title: Looking for movies that me-lonely can watch on Feb 14

commenti.body:
not sure if you’ve seen cronenbergs crash, but to me there’s an immense sadness to the picture, everyone’s sadness is portrayed really effectively through their perversion

if you already have seen that one or not interested in that one might i suggest ozu’s the only son, doesn’t so much deal with sexual frustration but i find the ideas of generationally immovable classes a really gut wrenching idea
sorry if not what you’re looking for, i think i differentiated the perversion you’re looking for and the sadness of love into 2 different camps, whereas I think you’re looking for that perfect blend

>ozu’s the only son

Yeah the blend is something rare to find, I agreee with your thoughts on crash. loved it. ozu's "the only son" is a new find. Thanks. will add it to my list.
yeah it’s very slow and meditative and doesn’t really unravel itself till it’s final shot, but that final shot is truly my fave of all time!
i will now shut my dirty mouth before i get overexcited and ruin the whole thing
wow. now that got me really curious. lol!

Todd Solondz is on the mind since casting for his new movie was just announced, and his Happiness is a brutally frank look at people trying to manage their sexuality and find genuine connection with another human being. The blackest of black comedies but extremely funny if you aren't averse to wallowing in the shit. It is probably in my top 25 movies all time and features a legendary Philip Seymour Hoffman performance.
good to hear, hopefully i convert another to the ozu cult
My immediate thought was The Virgin Suicides. Very much about yearning and dreams entrenched in the despair and loneliness of pubescent reality. Good luck, hope you have a good movie night.

>about struggle in finding a place in society, complicated and layered characters,  finding love, breakin up, carrying so much trauma and maybe finding some meaning in life that still keeps them going. 

The lobster 

Donnie Darko

I think they both qualify.

>Todd Solondz

this looks interesting. will definitely check. thanks!
oh thats a classic one. loved it. thanks
This is my favorite movie of all time. Great suggestion.

Chungking Express is really fantastic. It doesn’t cover nearly all you asked for, but you can find it on HBO. It’s a duel story of what it means to feel and want love and desire, and every small thing that happens between. It’s very funny and has a heavy noir feel to it.

Haneke's adaptation of "the piano teacher" was what I settled on for my Valentine's day viewing. It definitely ticks a few of your boxes, particularly the loneliness, sexual frustration, and layered characters. 


It's an incredible film and it will definitely shake you up and leave you feeling hollow.  


But a heads up that it's a very intense film, with scenes of sexual violence. Haneke's films really force the viewer to sit with deeply uncomfortable and confronting acts.
oh yeah that is one fine movie including the book on which the movie has been adapted. loved it. Thanks!

I’m pretty sure I’m speaking for everyone here by saying Predator (1987). It covers pretty much everything described above and it would be a nice time to remember the great Carl Weathers who passed away recently.
A Single Man (2009)  was great. thanks!

If you haven't already, I suggest trying Pedro Almodovar's Dolor y gloria (drama), Shinya Tsukamoto's Tetsuo The Iron Man (horror), Akira Kurosawa's The Quiet Duel (drama), Robert Eggers' The Lighthouse (horror?) or Gaspar Noe's LOVE (drama). I feel like these movies check a lot of those boxes.
Yorgos lanthimos' The Lobster might also be a good fit if you've not seen it. His film Alps too maybe.
Oh i loved lobster. Alps is a new find. will check that out, thanks!
amazing picks, particularly "the lighthouse". I am yet to watch Almodovar's Dolor y gloria. Will check! Thanks!

Based on the list of movies you’ve enjoyed, you might like Me and You and Everyone We Know, directed by Miranda July. It explores loneliness among a group of characters, and how loneliness is itself taboo. There are some moments of hope, but they feel earned. It’s been years since I’ve seen it, but a couple of scenes have stuck with me.

>Me and You

looks like a perfect fit for my mood. Thanks. will check it out
Oh my gawwwd! Yes ! I just rewatched Happiness this weekend after not having seen it in years. Boy did I forget what a cluster dysfunction and then some!
